docs.title: Black Beans
docs.text:
← All Recipes By AlexSideYield: 6 servingsCook: 45 min

Instant Pot black beans from dried. No soaking. The cinnamon is not optional.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 lb dried black beans, rinsed and picked through
  • 1 onion, diced
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 cinnamon stick (or 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon)
  • 1 tsp cumin
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 4 cups water or broth
  • Salt
  • Olive oil

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Set the Instant Pot to sauté. Add oil, cook the onion until soft, then the garlic for a minute.

  2. Add the beans, water, cumin, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Stir.

  3. Lock the lid, set to pressure cook on high for 30 minutes. Let it natural release for at least 15 minutes, then quick release the rest.

  4. Fish out the cinnamon stick and bay leaf. Salt generously — dried beans need more salt than you think. Taste and adjust.

docs.title: Breakfast Smoothie
docs.text:
← All Recipes By CarolynBreakfastYield: 2 smoothiesPrep: 5 min

The everyday one. Thick, cold, a little tart. Built to keep you full past mid-morning, not to leave you starving by ten.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 frozen banana (ripe and spotty, frozen in chunks)
  • 1 cup frozen mixed berries
  • 1/2 cup Greek yogurt
  • 1/2 cup milk or oat milk, plus more as needed
  • 1 tbsp nut butter or a handful of oats
  • Drizzle of honey, if your fruit isn't sweet
  • Tiny pinch of salt

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Use frozen fruit, not ice. The frozen banana is what makes it thick and creamy instead of cold and watery — freeze peeled chunks ahead of time so you always have some.

  2. Layer it smart: liquid first, then yogurt, then the frozen fruit on top. The blades catch the soft stuff first and everything blends smoother.

  3. Blend until completely smooth — no chunks, no frozen pocket spinning in place. If it stalls, add milk a splash at a time rather than just running the motor longer.

  4. Taste it. Too tart, add honey; too thick, more milk; too thin, a few more frozen berries. Pour into a cold glass and go.

docs.title: Chicken Salad
docs.text:
← All Recipes By NateEntreeYield: enough for a few sandwichesPrep: 15 min

Rotisserie chicken from the store is fine. Leftover roast chicken is better. Whatever you have works.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• Cooked chicken, shredded or chopped
  • Mayo — enough to make it creamy, probably more than you think
  • Salt and pepper
  • Lemon juice or a splash of pickle juice — one of these, not optional

Pick a direction and go with it:

Classic: celery, red onion, dijon, tarragon

Bright and herby: scallions, a lot of fresh dill, lemon juice instead of pickle juice

Tangy: pickles, dijon, scallions, a little hot sauce

Sweet and crunchy: grapes or apple, toasted walnuts or pecans, tarragon or chives

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Shred or chop the chicken. Smaller pieces hold together better in a sandwich, bigger chunks are more satisfying to eat plain. Pick based on how you're serving it.

  2. Mix in mayo until it looks right. Start with less, add more. You want it cohesive and a little creamy, not dry, not soupy.

  3. Salt and pepper, then taste it.

  4. Add whatever you picked from the list above. The acid — lemon juice or pickle juice — goes in last, just a little, and it makes a noticeable difference.

  5. Taste, adjust, done. Let it sit in the fridge for a bit if you can.

docs.title: Chili
docs.text:
← All Recipes By AlexEntreeYield: 8 servingsCook: 2 hrs

Ground turkey and ground beef, roughly half and half. The turkey keeps it from being heavy, the beef keeps it from being boring.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 lb ground turkey
  • 1 lb ground beef (80/20)
  • 1 large onion, diced
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2–3 poblano peppers
  • 2 cans diced tomatoes
  • 1 can kidney beans, drained
  • 1 can black beans, drained
  • 2 tbsp chili powder
  • 1 tbsp cumin
  • 1 tbsp cocoa powder
  • 1 cup brewed coffee (strong, black)
  • Salt and pepper
  • Olive oil

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Roast the poblanos yourself. Put them directly over a gas flame or under the broiler, turning until the skin is blistered and black all over. Drop them in a bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let them steam for ten minutes. Peel off the skin, remove the seeds, and chop them up.

  2. Brown the beef and turkey together in a big pot with some oil. Break it up, season it while it cooks. Pull it out and set it aside.

  3. In the same pot, cook the onion until soft, then the garlic for a minute. Add the chili powder, cumin, and cocoa powder and stir it around until it smells like something you want to eat.

  4. Add the tomatoes, beans, roasted poblanos, and the meat back in. Pour in the coffee. Stir it all together.

  5. Bring it up, then drop it to a low simmer. Let it go for at least an hour, longer if you can. It thickens up and the flavors settle in. Taste and adjust salt.

docs.title: Cinnamon Rolls
docs.text:
← All Recipes By CarolynBreakfastYield: 12 rollsCook: 25 min

Soft, gooey, cream-cheese-iced. The whole house smells like cinnamon for hours, which is the actual reason to make these.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
Dough

  • 4 cups flour
  • 1 packet (2 1/4 tsp) instant yeast
  • 1 cup warm milk
  • 1/3 cup sugar
  • 1/3 cup melted butter
  • 2 eggs
  • 1 tsp salt

Filling

  • 1/2 cup softened butter
  • 1 cup brown sugar
  • 2 tbsp cinnamon

Icing

  • 4 oz cream cheese, softened
  • 1 cup powdered sugar
  • 1/2 tsp vanilla
  • Splash of milk

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Warm the milk to wrist-temperature — warm, never hot, or it kills the yeast. Mix it with the yeast, sugar, melted butter, and eggs, then add the flour and salt. Knead until the dough is smooth and springs back when you poke it. Cover and let it rise until doubled, about an hour.

  2. Roll the dough out into a big rectangle. Spread the softened butter edge to edge, then scatter the brown sugar and cinnamon over every inch. It should already smell like a bakery.

  3. Roll it up tightly into a long log, seam-side down. Cut into 12 with a length of unflavored dental floss or a sharp knife, and nestle the rounds into a buttered pan, nearly touching.

  4. Let them puff up for another 30 minutes until they're swollen and bumping into each other. Bake at 350°F for 22–25 minutes until golden and the centers look just set — pull them while they still seem a touch underdone.

  5. Beat the cream cheese, powdered sugar, vanilla, and a splash of milk until smooth. Slather it over the rolls while they're still warm so it melts down into the swirls.

docs.title: Focaccia Bread (Alex's Version)
docs.text:
← All Recipes By AlexBreadYield: 9 piecesCook: 25 min

Same dimpled, olive-oil-drenched focaccia, but you jammy-roast a pan of cherry tomatoes and garlic first and press them into the top before it bakes. They collapse into little sweet-savory bombs. This is my version — there will be others.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 4 cups (500g) bread flour
  • 2 cups warm water
  • 2 tsp instant yeast
  • 2 tsp fine salt
  • 6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided, plus more for drizzling
  • 2 cups cherry tomatoes
  • 6 garlic cloves, smashed
  • Flaky salt and fresh rosemary, to finish

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Stir the flour, water, yeast, and fine salt together in a big bowl until it's a shaggy, sticky mess — no kneading. Drizzle a little oil over the top, cover, and let it rise until doubled and bubbly, about 1.5 hours (or overnight in the fridge).

  2. While it rises, cook the tomatoes and garlic down. Warm 3 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium-low, add the cherry tomatoes and smashed garlic, and let them slump and blister for 12–15 minutes. You want the tomatoes bursting and jammy and the garlic soft and golden — it'll smell sweet and toasty. Let it cool a little.

  3. Pour 3 tbsp oil into a 9x13 pan and slosh it around. Scrape the dough in and gently stretch it toward the corners; if it fights back, let it rest 10 minutes and try again. Cover and let it puff for another 30–40 minutes until pillowy.

  4. Oil your fingers and dimple the dough all over, going all the way down. Spoon the tomatoes and garlic over the top, pressing them into the dimples along with their oil. Finish with flaky salt and rosemary.

  5. Bake at 450°F for 22–25 minutes until deep golden and the edges are crisp. It should sound hollow and the bottom should be lacquered from the oil. Cool in the pan a few minutes, then lift out.

docs.title: Focaccia Bread (Ceci's Version)
docs.text:
← All Recipes By CeciBreadYield: 9 piecesCook: 25 min

Same dimpled, olive-oil-drenched focaccia, except you spoon chili crisp oil into every dimple before it bakes. The oil crisps the crust and the little flakes and fried garlic bits toast in the heat. Crunchy, spicy, savory. This is my version — there will be others.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 4 cups (500g) bread flour
  • 2 cups warm water
  • 2 tsp instant yeast
  • 2 tsp fine salt
  • 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for the pan
  • 3–4 tbsp chili crisp oil (the crunchy kind — Lao Gan Ma, Fly By Jing, whatever you like), well stirred
  • Flaky salt and thinly sliced scallions, to finish

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Stir the flour, water, yeast, and fine salt together in a big bowl until it's a shaggy, sticky mess — no kneading. Drizzle a little olive oil over the top, cover, and let it rise until doubled and bubbly, about 1.5 hours (or overnight in the fridge).

  2. Pour a good glug of olive oil into a 9x13 pan and slosh it around. Scrape the dough in and gently stretch it toward the corners; if it fights back, let it rest 10 minutes and try again. Cover and let it puff for another 30–40 minutes until pillowy.

  3. Oil your fingers and dimple the dough all over, pressing all the way down. Stir the chili crisp well so you get both the oil and the crunchy bits, then spoon it into the dimples — let it pool. Finish with a little flaky salt.

  4. Bake at 450°F for 22–25 minutes until deep golden and the edges are crisp. Watch the chili flakes near the end — you want them toasty and fragrant, not scorched. It should smell like garlic and chili and sound hollow when you tap it.

  5. Cool in the pan a few minutes, then lift out and scatter the scallions over the top for a fresh, sharp bite against the heat.

docs.title: Gazpacho
docs.text:
← All Recipes By CeciStarterYield: 6 servingsPrep: 20 min

Cold tomato soup for when it's too hot to cook. The blender does the work and the fridge does the rest.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 2 lbs ripe tomatoes, roughly chopped
  • 1 cucumber, peeled and chopped
  • 1 green pepper, seeded and chopped
  • 1/2 red onion, chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic
  • 1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
  • 2 tbsp sherry vinegar
  • 1 cup day-old bread, torn into pieces and soaked in water
  • Salt to taste
  • Cold water as needed

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Soak the bread in water until soft, then squeeze it out. Throw everything — tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, onion, garlic, bread — into a blender and blend until smooth.

  2. Drizzle in the olive oil and sherry vinegar while it's running. Season with salt. If it's too thick, add cold water a little at a time until it pours easily but still feels substantial. Strain it if you want it silky, skip if you like some texture.

  3. Refrigerate for at least two hours — it needs to be very cold. Serve with a drizzle of olive oil and whatever you want on top: chopped cucumber, pepper, croutons.

docs.title: Granola
docs.text:
← All Recipes By EmilyBreakfastYield: 8 servingsCook: 35 min

Olive oil instead of butter. Pistachios and walnuts. This is the granola.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 3 cups old-fashioned oats
  • 1 cup raw pistachios, roughly chopped
  • 1 cup raw walnuts, roughly chopped
  • 1/3 cup olive oil
  • 1/3 cup maple syrup or honey
  • 1/4 cup brown sugar
  • 1 tsp vanilla
  • 1/2 tsp cinnamon
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • Dried fruit (optional, add after baking)

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Heat the oven to 325°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment.

  2. Mix the oats, pistachios, and walnuts in a big bowl. In a smaller bowl, whisk together the olive oil, maple syrup, brown sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt.

  3. Pour the wet over the dry and stir until everything is coated. Spread it out on the baking sheet in an even layer. Press it down a little — this is how you get clusters.

  4. Bake for about 30 minutes, stirring once halfway through. It should be golden and fragrant. It'll crisp up more as it cools, so pull it when it still looks slightly underdone.

  5. Let it cool completely on the pan without touching it. Break it into pieces. Add dried fruit if you want it.

docs.title: Kale Caesar Salad
docs.text:
← All Recipes By KunalSideYield: 6–8 servingsPrep: 15 minCook: 30 min

A Caesar that won't turn to soup. The kale holds up, the croutons are homemade, and the dressing hides six anchovies you'll never see coming.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 2 bunches Tuscan or curly kale (about 1 lb), stems stripped, leaves roughly chopped
  • 5 tbsp olive oil, divided
  • 5 oz hearty bread, torn into chunks
  • Salt and pepper
  • 2/3 cup mayonnaise
  • 6 anchovy filets
  • 1 garlic clove, minced
  • 3/4 cup finely grated Parmesan (about 1 1/2 oz)
  • 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce
  • 2 tbsp lemon juice (about 1 lemon)
  • 1 small white onion or 2 shallots, thinly sliced

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Strip the kale off its stems, tear the leaves into a big bowl, and pour over 3 tbsp of the oil. Massage it in with your hands for a couple minutes — the leaves should darken, turn silky, and shrink down by half. Set aside.

  2. Croutons: pulse the bread with the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a food processor until you've got pea-sized crumbs, then season with salt and pepper. Spread on a sheet pan and bake at 350°F until pale gold and crisp, about 20 minutes. You'll smell toast when they're ready.

  3. Wipe out the processor and add the mayo, anchovies, garlic, Parmesan, Worcestershire, and lemon juice. Blitz until smooth and creamy. Taste — it should be punchy and a little salty; nudge with more salt and pepper if it needs it.

  4. Toss the kale with the sliced onion, all the dressing, and half the croutons until every leaf is coated. Scatter the rest of the croutons on top and serve.

docs.title: Larb
docs.text:
← All Recipes By AlexEntreeYield: 4 servingsCook: 25 min

Ground turkey larb. The toasted rice powder is the whole thing — don't skip it, don't buy it pre-made.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 lb ground turkey
  • 1/4 cup uncooked jasmine rice (for toasting)
  • 3 tbsp fish sauce
  • 3 tbsp lime juice (about 2 limes)
  • 1 tsp sugar
  • 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes or dried chili flakes
  • 3–4 shallots, thinly sliced
  • Handful of fresh mint leaves
  • Handful of fresh cilantro
  • Scallions, sliced
  • Butter lettuce leaves for serving

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Toast the rice. Dry skillet, medium heat, toss the raw rice in and shake it around for several minutes until it's golden brown and smells nutty. Let it cool, then grind it in a mortar and pestle or spice grinder until it's a coarse powder. This is what makes it larb.

  2. Cook the turkey in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it goes. No oil needed — it'll render enough. Season lightly with salt while it cooks.

  3. While the meat cooks, mix the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and chili flakes together.

  4. When the turkey is cooked through, take it off the heat. Pour the dressing over it and toss. Add the shallots, most of the herbs, and the toasted rice powder. Toss again.

  5. Serve in lettuce cups with the rest of the herbs on top.

docs.title: Matzoh Ball Soup
docs.text:
← All Recipes By EmilyEntreeYield: 6 servingsCook: 1 hr

Fluffy matzoh balls in good chicken broth. The hardest part is leaving the lid alone.

docs.title: Matzoh Balls
docs.text:
• 1 cup matzoh meal
  • 4 eggs, beaten
  • 1/4 cup schmaltz (or vegetable oil, but schmaltz)
  • 1/4 cup broth or seltzer
  • 1 tsp salt
  • Pinch of white pepper

docs.title: Soup
docs.text:
• 8 cups good chicken broth — homemade or the best you can buy
  • 2 carrots, peeled and sliced into rounds
  • 2 stalks celery, sliced
  • Fresh dill for serving

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Mix the eggs, schmaltz, broth, salt, and pepper together. Stir in the matzoh meal until just combined. Don't overwork it. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes — the mixture needs to firm up.

  2. While the batter chills, bring the chicken broth to a simmer with the carrots and celery.

  3. Wet your hands and roll the batter into balls, about the size of a walnut. They'll puff up, so keep them on the smaller side.

  4. Drop them gently into the simmering broth. Cover the pot and don't lift the lid for 20 minutes. They need the steam.

  5. After 20 minutes, check one. It should be fluffy all the way through, no dense center. Serve with fresh dill on top.

docs.title: Peanut GalleryMore from Emily
docs.text:

docs.title: Meatloaf
docs.text:
← All Recipes By BenEntreeYield: 6 servingsCook: 1 hr

Plain, classic, ketchup-glazed. Nothing in here is trying to surprise you.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 2 lbs ground beef (80/20)
  • 1 cup breadcrumbs
  • 2 eggs, beaten
  • 1/2 cup milk
  • 1 onion, finely diced
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1/2 tsp black pepper
  • 1/2 tsp onion powder

docs.title: Glaze
docs.text:
• 1/2 cup ketchup
  • 2 tbsp brown sugar
  • 1 tbsp mustard

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Heat the oven to 375°F. Mix the breadcrumbs and milk in a bowl and let it sit for a few minutes so the crumbs soak it up.

  2. Combine the beef, eggs, soaked breadcrumbs, onion, garlic, Worcestershire, salt, pepper, and onion powder. Mix it with your hands until it's just combined. Don't overwork it or it'll be dense.

  3. Shape it into a loaf on a lined baking sheet or press it into a loaf pan. Free-form on the sheet gets better edges.

  4. Mix the ketchup, brown sugar, and mustard together. Spread it over the top of the loaf.

  5. Bake for about 50–60 minutes until it reads 160°F in the center. Let it rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

docs.title: Milk Bread
docs.text:
← All Recipes By KunalBreadYield: 1 loafCook: 35 min

Pillowy Japanese-style shokupan. The trick is the tangzhong — a quick cooked flour paste that keeps the crumb soft for days.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 2 tbsp bread flour + 1/2 cup milk (for the tangzhong)
  • 2 1/2 cups bread flour
  • 1/4 cup sugar
  • 2 1/4 tsp instant yeast
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1/2 cup warm milk
  • 1 egg
  • 3 tbsp soft butter
  • 1 egg beaten with a splash of milk (for the wash)

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Make the tangzhong: whisk the 2 tbsp flour into the 1/2 cup milk in a small pot over medium heat, stirring constantly until it thickens into a loose paste you can draw a line through — about 2 minutes. Let it cool to warm.

  2. In a big bowl, mix the bread flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. Add the warm milk, egg, and the cooled tangzhong. Mix into a shaggy dough, then knead. Once it comes together, work in the soft butter a bit at a time. Keep kneading until it's smooth, tacky, and stretches thin without tearing — about 10 minutes.

  3. Cover and let it rise somewhere warm until doubled and puffy, roughly 1 hour. Press a finger in; the dent should spring back slowly.

  4. Punch it down, divide into 3 or 4 pieces, roll each flat, fold, and roll into logs. Tuck them seam-side down into a buttered loaf pan. Cover and proof again until they crest just over the rim, about 45 minutes.

  5. Brush with the egg wash and bake at 350°F until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped, 30–35 minutes. Turn it out and cool before you tear in — the steam is still setting the crumb.

docs.title: Mojo Pork
docs.text:
← All Recipes By CeciEntreeYield: 8 servingsCook: 3–4 hrs (oven) / 1 hr (Instant Pot)

Slow-cooked pork shoulder drenched in a garlicky citrus mojo. The crust at the end is non-negotiable — that's where the magic lives.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 4 lbs pork shoulder, cut into 3–4 large chunks
  • 10 cloves garlic, minced or mashed
  • 1 cup sour orange juice (or 3/4 cup orange juice + 1/4 cup lime juice)
  • 1/4 cup olive oil
  • 2 tsp ground cumin
  • 1 tbsp dried oregano
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1/2 tsp black pepper
  • 1 large onion, sliced into thick rings

docs.title: Instructions (Instant Pot)
docs.text:
1. Mash the garlic with the salt into a rough paste — a mortar and pestle is ideal, a fork and cutting board works. Mix it with the sour orange juice, olive oil, cumin, and oregano. Score the pork chunks deeply with a knife, then pour the mojo all over and into every cut. Marinate at least an hour, overnight if you can.

  2. Set the Instant Pot to sauté and get it hot. Pull the pork out of the marinade (save that liquid) and sear each piece until it's golden brown on at least two sides. It should smell like toasted garlic and cumin. Don't rush this.

  3. Lay the onion rings on the bottom, nestle the pork on top, and pour in the reserved marinade. Lock the lid and pressure cook on high for 45 minutes, then let it natural release for 15 minutes before venting.

  4. Pull the pork out and shred it with two forks — it should fall apart with almost no effort. Spoon some of the cooking liquid over the shredded meat to keep it juicy.

  5. Spread the shredded pork on a sheet pan and broil for 3–5 minutes until the edges get dark and crispy. Watch it closely — you want charred tips, not ash. Squeeze fresh lime over the top before serving.

docs.title: Instructions (Stove & Oven)
docs.text:
1. Mash the garlic with the salt into a rough paste — a mortar and pestle is ideal, a fork and cutting board works. Mix it with the sour orange juice, olive oil, cumin, and oregano. Score the pork chunks deeply with a knife, then pour the mojo all over and into every cut. Marinate at least an hour, overnight if you can.

  2. Heat a Dutch oven over medium-high heat with a splash of oil. Pull the pork out of the marinade (save that liquid) and sear each piece until it's golden brown on at least two sides. It should smell like toasted garlic and cumin. Don't rush this.

  3. Lay the onion rings on the bottom, put the pork back in, and pour the reserved marinade over everything. Add a splash of water if the liquid doesn't come at least halfway up the meat. Bring to a simmer, cover with the lid, and slide it into a 325°F oven.

  4. Braise for 3 to 3.5 hours, flipping the pork once halfway through. It's done when a fork slides through the meat like butter. Pull it out and shred it with two forks, spooning the braising liquid over the meat as you go.

  5. Spread the shredded pork on a sheet pan and broil for 3–5 minutes until the edges get dark and crispy. Watch it closely — you want charred tips, not ash. Squeeze fresh lime over the top before serving.

docs.title: Paella
docs.text:
← All Recipes By CeciEntreeYield: 6 servingsCook: 45 min

Paella valenciana — chicken, beans, saffron rice, and a toasted crust on the bottom worth fighting over. You need a wide pan; the rice should sit in a thin layer, not a deep pile.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 2 cups bomba or other short-grain Spanish rice
  • 1 lb chicken thighs, cut into pieces
  • A big handful of flat green beans, trimmed
  • 1 cup butter beans or lima beans
  • 1 tomato, grated
  • 1 tsp sweet paprika (pimentón)
  • A good pinch of saffron
  • 5 cups warm chicken broth
  • Olive oil and salt
  • A sprig of rosemary
  • Lemon wedges, for serving

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Heat olive oil in the widest pan you own. Brown the chicken hard on all sides, salting as you go, then push it out to the edges. You want real color here — that's where the flavor starts.

  2. Add the green beans and butter beans, then the grated tomato and paprika. Cook it down until the tomato darkens, goes jammy, and smells sweet — just don't let the paprika scorch or it turns bitter.

  3. Pour in the warm broth, crumble in the saffron, drop in the rosemary, and bring it to a strong simmer. Taste it: it should be a touch too salty right now, because the rice will soak that up and mellow it.

  4. Scatter the rice in evenly and spread it flat. Now do not stir it again — ever. Stirring releases starch and you'll have risotto. Keep it at a steady bubble, turning the pan for even cooking, for about 18 minutes until the liquid is gone.

  5. Crank the heat the last minute or two to build the socarrat, the toasted crust on the bottom — listen for a faint crackle and smell for toasty, not burnt. Rest it under foil for 5 minutes, then serve with lemon.

docs.title: Quesadilla
docs.text:
← All Recipes By TimEntreeYield: 2 quesadillasCook: 15 min

The fast lunch that lives or dies on two things: the cheese and the heat. Get those right and the rest is just decoration.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 2 large flour tortillas
  • 2 cups shredded cheese (Monterey jack, Oaxaca, or a jack-cheddar mix)
  • Cooked filling: shredded chicken, sautéed peppers and onion, whatever you've got
  • A little butter or oil
  • Salt
  • For serving: salsa, sour cream, lime, hot sauce

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Grate your own cheese off the block. Pre-shredded is coated in starch so it doesn't clump in the bag — which also means it never melts into that proper gooey pull. This is the one non-negotiable.

  2. Set a skillet over medium and butter it lightly. Lay a tortilla down, scatter cheese over half, add your filling, then a little more cheese on top — cheese against both sides of the fold glues the whole thing shut. Fold it over.

  3. Listen for a steady, gentle sizzle, not a violent one. Too hot and the outside chars before the cheese gives up. Press down softly with a spatula.

  4. Flip when the underside is golden and freckled with brown spots, about 2–3 minutes a side. The second side always goes faster, so watch it.

  5. Slide it out and wait a full minute — molten cheese is a trap and you know it. Cut into wedges and serve with salsa and a squeeze of lime.

docs.title: Rice Krispy Treats
docs.text:
← All Recipes By EmilyDessertYield: 12 squaresCook: 15 min

The classic, with two small upgrades: a pinch of salt and a little vanilla.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 6 cups Rice Krispies cereal
  • 1 bag (10 oz) marshmallows
  • 3 tbsp butter
  • Pinch of salt
  • 1/2 tsp vanilla (optional but better)

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Melt the butter in a big pot over low heat. Add the marshmallows and stir constantly until they're completely melted and smooth. Take it off the heat.

  2. Stir in the salt and vanilla if you're using it. Pour in the cereal and fold it together gently. You want every piece coated but you don't want to crush them.

  3. Press into a buttered 9x13 pan. Don't press too hard — if you compact them, they'll be dense and chewy instead of light and crispy. Use a piece of wax paper or wet hands to pat them down.

  4. Let them cool completely before cutting. Or don't. Nobody actually waits.

docs.title: Ropa Vieja
docs.text:
← All Recipes By CeciEntreeYield: 8 servingsCook: 20 min

Shredded flank steak simmered with tomato, peppers, and wine. It starts with meat you've already cooked, so it comes together fast.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 2 lbs flank steak, cooked ahead of time in broth or soup
  • 1/3 cup oil
  • 1 onion, thinly sliced into rounds
  • 2 cloves garlic, crushed
  • 1 large ají (cubanelle or green pepper), cut into strips
  • 1 can tomato sauce
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1/2 cup dry white wine
  • 1 can roasted red peppers (pimientos morrones)

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Shred the cooked flank steak into thin threads or strips with your hands.

  2. Slice the onion into thin rounds and cut the pepper into strips. Crush the garlic and fry it in the hot oil, then add the onion. Once softened, add the pepper and cook a bit more.

  3. Add the shredded meat and all remaining ingredients — tomato sauce, bay leaf, salt, wine. The roasted peppers can go in chopped, blended into the sauce, or saved whole to lay on top as garnish — your call. Stir to combine.

  4. Cover and simmer over low heat for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally so it doesn't stick. You'll know it's ready when it smells deep and savory and the sauce clings to the meat.

  5. Serve with white rice and a fresh salad.

docs.title: Sourdough Bread
docs.text:
← All Recipes By CarolynBreadYield: 1 loafCook: 45 min

A basic country loaf. This is mostly waiting — the hands-on time is small, the patience is large. Start the morning before you want bread.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 500g bread flour
  • 350g water, room temperature
  • 100g active sourdough starter (bubbly and risen, not flat)
  • 10g salt

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Mix the flour and water with your hands until there are no dry bits left, then let it rest 30–60 minutes. Add the starter and salt and squish everything through your fingers until it goes from shaggy to smooth and tacky — it should grab your hand a little.

  2. Over the next 2–3 hours, do a few rounds of stretch-and-folds: wet your hand, grab one side of the dough, stretch it up and fold it over, turn the bowl, repeat four times. It'll feel slack at first and slowly turn smooth, pillowy, and strong.

  3. Let it bulk ferment at room temperature until it's risen by about half, looks domed, and has a few bubbles on top. Give the bowl a jiggle — it should wobble like it's alive.

  4. Tip it out, shape it into a tight ball by dragging it across the counter to build tension on the surface, and settle it seam-up in a floured bowl or banneton. Cover and cold-proof in the fridge overnight (8–14 hours).

  5. Bake in a screaming-hot Dutch oven at 500°F: score the top with one confident half-inch slash, lid on for 20 minutes, then lid off and drop to 450°F for 20–25 more until it's deep brown and sounds hollow when you tap the bottom. Cool it completely — listen for the crust crackling as it sets.

docs.title: Spanish Tortilla
docs.text:
← All Recipes By CeciEntreeYield: 6 servingsCook: 30 min

Tortilla de patatas. Potatoes, eggs, onion, olive oil — that's the whole list, and it's somehow one of the best things you can make. Good warm, even better at room temperature.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 5 medium potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
  • 1 large onion, thinly sliced
  • 6 eggs
  • Olive oil, enough to nearly cover the potatoes (about 1 1/2 cups)
  • Salt

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Heat a generous pool of olive oil in a skillet over medium-low. Slip in the potatoes and onion, salt them, and poach gently — they should bubble softly, never crisp up or brown. Stir now and then until they're meltingly soft, about 20 minutes.

  2. Drain the potatoes and onion in a sieve, saving that good oil. Let them cool for a couple of minutes so they don't scramble the eggs on contact.

  3. Beat the eggs with a good pinch of salt in a big bowl, then fold the warm potatoes in. Let it sit 5–10 minutes — the potatoes drink up the egg, and that's the secret to a tortilla that holds together instead of falling apart.

  4. Heat a few spoonfuls of the reserved oil in a nonstick pan over medium. Pour everything in, settle it into an even round, and cook until the edges set and the bottom turns golden — slide a spatula underneath to peek.

  5. Now the flip: cover the pan with a plate, turn the whole thing out onto it, then slide it back in to set the other side for a few minutes. Keep the center just barely soft — you want jammy, not dry.
